home.manifestoCol1: A network of companies, shared workspaces, an education that doesn't end in the classroom: they are not elements alongside the course of study — they are an integral part of it. Studying and entering the industry happen in the same place.
home.manifestoCol2: Students work side by side with people already in the industry — in the same network of companies, in the same spaces. Not an internship at the end of the course, but a constant condition: education stays anchored to what the market demands today, not to a syllabus fixed years ago.

storiaItems.title: Foundation
storiaItems.text: In 1999 Massimiliano Magagni and Susanna Goldoni founded Italy's first school to bring the US teaching approach to popular music to Bologna, in partnership with the Los Angeles Music Academy — now the Los Angeles College of Music. The Bachelor's degree is awarded in partnership with Coventry University: an international qualification, not a local certificate.

storiaItems.title: Offering
storiaItems.text: Over twenty-five years the course offering has grown from instrumental performance to composition for film and video games, through to film production and sound engineering.

storiaItems.title: The new name
storiaItems.text: In 2021 Music Academy became Creative Hub Academy: Creative Hub Bologna was also born, the incubator that is today the Innovation area.

storiaItems.title: Awards
storiaItems.text: The "L'Europa è QUI" award in 2020, ISO 9001:EA37 certification.

storiaItems.title: Research
storiaItems.text: With the University of Bologna's DAMS, Tecnopolo CNR and Clust-ER Create, the Academy experiments with technologies applied to music and audiovisual production and distribution.

storiaItems.title: The campus
storiaItems.text: Three recording, mastering and post-production studios, isobox, a live room, four production boxes, a main hall with virtual theatre, a VR/AR room, a radio studio. Around two million euros of investment, co-funded by the Emilia-Romagna Region.

teachersIntro: Creative Hub Academy's teachers are working professionals in the music industry, not teachers describing a job they no longer do. What you bring into the classroom, they're doing right now, outside these walls: on tour, in the studio, on stage.
Among them Angela Madonia, a vocal coach familiar to Amici audiences, and Stefania Martin, who has worked alongside Renato Zero and Mina.
academy.inMemoriaText: Bologna also counted Celso Valli among its teachers, the arranger and producer behind the sound of Vasco Rossi, Laura Pausini, Mina and Eros Ramazzotti. He passed away in 2025. What he taught here still shapes the way the Academy works today.

faq.title: The questions you ask us before choosing.

items.q: What is the difference between a Bachelor and an Italian degree?
items.a: The Bachelor is the first-cycle university degree of the British and European system: same level, awarded by a foreign university. What changes is the approach: more hours of practice, small classes, teachers who work in the industry.

We meet at an open day or an interview, then you send your application with a piece of your work and take an audition or an interview in your field. We are not looking for people who already know everything: we are looking for people with a direction.
Lessons are scheduled in time slots agreed with your tutor, and part of the programme can be followed online. Check with us that it fits your schedule before enrolling.

items.q: Do I need experience or equipment already?
items.a: You need a foundation in your field, not a CV. On site you have recording studios, production boxes and the SSL control room. For studying at home, we tell you what you need, course by course.

items.q: How much does it cost, and can I pay in instalments?
items.a: The fee depends on the course. You pay in zero-interest instalments, with discounts for early enrolment and merit scholarships. Ask us for the details of the course you are interested in.
